references.text: God's promise to Jacob at Bethel to be with him wherever he went, which directly corresponds to 'who was with me on the way I walked'.
Jacob's vow at Bethel to honor God there, now fulfilled as he returns to build an altar.
God identifies Himself as the God of Bethel and commands Jacob to return to his homeland, forming the background for the journey to Bethel.
Jacob's distress and fear when he heard that Esau was coming against him, part of the background for 'who answered me on my day of trouble'.
Abram builds an altar to the Lord at Bethel, showing the early tradition of worship at this place.
Hosea reminds us that God found Jacob at Bethel and spoke with him there, confirming Bethel's significance in Jacob's life.
Thematic parallel between Abraham's and Jacob's establishment of altars in the Bethel area as a place for worship.
Theological contrast between Bethel as a place of God's grace (Jacob) and judgment against idolatry (Amos).
Genesis 35:3 is a concrete fulfillment of the principle in Exodus 20:24 that God meets people where He allows His name to be remembered.
Theological contrast between the proper use of an altar to honor God (Jacob) and the dangers of building extra altars (Joshua).
